questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
questions.option_4: Article 19 – Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech
questions.solution:
The correctly matched pair is Article 19 – Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech. Article 19 guarantees six freedoms, including speech and expression.

Corrections: Article 17 is for the Abolition of Untouchability, Article 18 is for the Abolition of Titles, Article 14 is for Equality before Law, and Article 15 prohibits discrimination.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India mentions that law declared by Supreme Court is binding on all courts?
questions.solution:
Article 141 of the Indian Constitution stipulates that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India. This ensures judicial consistency and the principle of stare decisis (precedents) across the country.

Related: Article 142 deals with the enforcement of decrees and orders of the Supreme Court to provide 'complete justice'.

questions.question: Article 323 of the Indian Constitution deals with ________.
questions.option_3: power to extend functions of Public Services Commissions
questions.solution:
Article 323 deals with the reports of Public Service Commissions. It mandates that the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) must present an annual report to the President, while State Commissions present theirs to the Governor, detailing the work done by them.

Note: Articles 315-323 cover various aspects of the Public Service Commissions.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the State Executive?
A. Article 152 of the Indian Constitution states ‘Unless the context otherwise requires, the expression ‘State’ does not include Jammu and Kashmir’.
B. The 7th Constitutional Amendment Act has provided for the appointment of the same person as Governor for two or more states.
C. The Supreme Court clearly mentioned that the office of the Governor is under the control of the Central Government.
questions.solution: Statements A and B only are correct. (A) Article 152 defines 'State' and historically excluded J&K from certain general provisions. (B) The 7th Amendment Act (1956) allowed the same person to be Governor of multiple states. Statement C is incorrect because the Supreme Court held that the Governor's office is an independent constitutional office and not a subordinate post under the Central Government.

questions.question:
Which among the following statements about judicial review in India are correct?
A. Judicial review means that the courts of law have the power of testing the validity of legislative as well as other governmental action with reference to the provisions of the Constitution.
B. Under Article 23 of the Indian Constitution, the compulsion of judicial review was described in the Fundamental Rights in Part III.
C. The power of judicial review is significantly vested upon the High Courts and the Supreme Court of India.
questions.solution:
Statements A and C only are correct. (A) Judicial review allows courts to test the constitutionality of laws. (C) This power is primarily vested in the Supreme Court (Art 32) and High Courts (Art 226). Statement B is incorrect because Article 13 (not 23) is considered the backbone of judicial review in the Fundamental Rights section.

Note: Article 23 relates to the prohibition of forced labor.

questions.question: The Indian Constitution originally consisted of ______ Articles.
questions.solution:
The Indian Constitution originally consisted of 395 Articles, 22 Parts, and 8 Schedules. It was adopted on November 26, 1949.

Additional Info: Due to various amendments over the years, the number of articles has increased significantly (over 448), though they retain their original numbering with suffixes like 21A, 51A, etc.

questions.question: What is the duty of the Chief Minister, as mentioned under Article 167 of the Indian Constitution?
questions.option_1: Appointment of Advocate General of the state in consultation with Attorney general.
questions.option_2: Appointment of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.
questions.option_3: Appointment and removal of Council of the Ministers.
questions.option_4: Communication of all decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor.
questions.solution:
According to Article 167, it is the duty of the Chief Minister to communicate all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to the administration of the affairs of the State and proposals for legislation to the Governor.

Role: The CM acts as the primary link between the Cabinet and the Governor.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution prohibits religious instructions in any state-funded educational institution?
questions.solution:
Article 28 of the Indian Constitution prohibits religious instructions in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds. It ensures the secular character of state-run education.

Note: Article 29 and 30 deal with the protection of interests and the right of minorities to establish educational institutions.

questions.question: Which of the following is mentioned in the Preamble of the Constitution of India?
questions.option_4: Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship
questions.solution:
The Preamble mentions Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship.

Corrections: It mentions Equality of status and of opportunity (not employment), Fraternity assuring the dignity of the individual (not just human dignity), and Justice: social, economic and political (not administrative).

questions.question: Which amendment of Indian Constitution removed the right to property from the list of fundamental rights?
questions.solution:
The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 removed the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights. It was previously under Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31.

Current Status: It is now a legal right under Article 300A in Part XII of the Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT come under the Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India?
questions.option_1: Uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
questions.option_2: Cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom
questions.option_3: Safeguard public property and to abjure violence
questions.solution:
To Exercise adult franchise (voting) is a Constitutional/Legal right, but it is NOT listed as one of the 11 Fundamental Duties under Article 51A.

Included Duties: Protecting sovereignty, following national ideals, and safeguarding public property are all explicit duties prescribed for citizens.

questions.question: Which was the first country to incorporate Fundamental Duties in its Constitution?
questions.solution:
The USSR (Soviet Union) was the first major country to incorporate a comprehensive list of Fundamental Duties in its Constitution. India's Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A) were largely inspired by the Soviet model during the 42nd Amendment.

Note: Most democratic constitutions (like the US or Canada) focus primarily on rights.

questions.question: From which country were the Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution borrowed?
questions.solution: The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) were borrowed from the Irish Constitution (which in turn had taken them from the Spanish Constitution). These are guidelines for the government to ensure social and economic justice.

questions.question: The feature of fundamental duties in the Indian Constitution is adopted from which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The feature of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution was adopted from the Soviet Union (USSR). They were added in 1976 to provide a balance between the rights enjoyed by citizens and their obligations toward the nation.

Additional Info: This was done on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

questions.question: India borrowed the DPSP from the _______ Constitution.
questions.solution:
India borrowed the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) from the Irish Constitution. The DPSP are contained in Part IV (Articles 36-51).

Note: These principles are fundamental in the governance of the country but are not enforceable by any court.

questions.question: Part 3 of the Indian Constitution enlists how many groups of Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution:
Part III of the Indian Constitution enlists 6 groups of Fundamental Rights: 1. Right to Equality, 2. Right to Freedom, 3. Right against Exploitation, 4. Right to Freedom of Religion, 5. Cultural and Educational Rights, and 6. Right to Constitutional Remedies.

Note: There were originally 7, but Right to Property was removed.

questions.question: Under which Constitutional Amendment, the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children from the age of six to fourteen years?.
questions.solution:
Under the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, Article 21A was inserted, making free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years.

Additional Info: This amendment also changed the DPSP (Article 45) and added the 11th Fundamental Duty.

questions.question: What do you understand by ‘dual citizenship’ as in the case of the US?
questions.option_2: Citizenship of two states alongwith two countries
questions.option_3: Citizenship of two states simultaneously with two countries
questions.option_4: Citizenship of a country alongwith that of a constituent State, where one resides/born
questions.solution:
In the US, dual citizenship refers to the system where a person is a citizen of the country (USA) and simultaneously a citizen of the specific state (e.g., California or Texas) where they reside.

Contrast: India follows Single Citizenship, meaning an Indian is a citizen of India only, regardless of the state they live in.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding Parliamentary Committees?
A. A minister cannot be a member of the Public Accounts Committee.
B. The members of the Estimates Committee are nominated by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
C. A minister can be a member of the Estimates Committee if he is nominated by the Speaker.
D. A member of the Committee on Public Undertakings will have tenure of 2 years.
questions.solution:
Statement A only is correct. A minister cannot be a member of the Public Accounts Committee (or the Estimates Committee/PUC) to ensure the independence of legislative oversight.

Corrections: (B) Estimates Committee members are elected by Lok Sabha, not nominated. (D) Members of the Committee on Public Undertakings have a tenure of 1 year.

questions.question: The centre of a cyclone is a calm area. It is called the ______ of the storm.
questions.solution:
The center of a cyclone is a calm area known as the 'eye' of the storm. It is a region of mostly calm weather found at the center of strong tropical cyclones.

Characteristics: The eye is roughly circular and typically 30–65 km in diameter, surrounded by the 'eyewall', the most dangerous part of the storm.

questions.question: Who, being the Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Armed Forces, takes the salute of different regiments of the armed forces during the march-past on Republic Day?
questions.solution:
The President of India is the Supreme Commander of the Indian Armed Forces. During the Republic Day parade, the President takes the salute as the Commander-in-Chief.

Note: This ceremonial role signifies the civilian control over the military in a democracy.

questions.question: The Governor of an Indian state before entering upon his office takes an oath or affirmation before ________.
questions.option_1: the Chief Minister of the concerned state
questions.option_2: the Chief Justice of the High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to the State
questions.solution:
The Governor of a state takes the oath before the Chief Justice of the High Court of that state (or the senior-most judge in their absence). This is specified under Article 159 of the Constitution.

Note: This is the state-level equivalent of the President taking the oath before the CJI.

questions.question: Which of the following can make provisions for Ancillary powers of the Supreme Court?
questions.solution: The Parliament of India has the power to make provisions for the Ancillary powers of the Supreme Court under Article 140. This allows the Supreme Court to exercise its jurisdiction more effectively for the purpose of achieving the objects of the Constitution.

questions.question: Fundamental duties are ___________ and not enforceable by law but are taken into account by the courts while adjudicating any matter.
questions.solution: Fundamental duties are statutory in the sense that Parliament can enforce them through specific laws (like the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act). While the duties themselves are non-justiciable (cannot be directly enforced by courts), they serve as a guide for interpreting laws and determining the constitutionality of legislation.

questions.question: In India Who among the following has the power to pardon, reprieve or commute the punishment of any criminal?
questions.solution:
The President of India has the power to pardon, reprieve, respite, or commute sentences under Article 72. This includes cases involving court-martials and death sentences.

Note: The Governor has similar powers under Article 161, but cannot pardon a death sentence or deal with court-martial cases.
